question: Which of the following is NOT correct regarding the periodic table?

options.text: There are 18 periods and 7 groups in the periodic table.
Group 2 elements are called alkaline earth metals.
There are 7 periods and 18 groups in the periodic table.
Noble gases are included in group 18.

solution:
The correct answer is **There are 18 periods and 7 groups in the periodic table.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the Modern Periodic Table, there is 18 vertical columns called Groups and 7 horizontal rows called Periods.
 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **Mistake Points__** 
 __
 
• Hence, the 1st statement is incorrect and 3rd statement is correct. 
 
 
 
• Group 1 elements are called Alkali Metals and Group 2 elements are known as Alkaline Earth Metals, hence statement 2 is correct.
 
• Noble or Inert Gases are placed in **Group 18**, hence statement 4 is **correct**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The modern periodic table** is a tabular arrangement of the **chemical elements**, organized by their **atomic number, electron configuration, and recurring chemical properties**.
 
• It was first developed by Russian chemist** Dmitri Mendeleev** in **1869**, and has since been expanded and refined by numerous scientists.
 
• The table is divided into** rows called periods** and **columns called groups or families**.
 
• Elements in the** same group** have **similar chemical properties**, while elements in the **same period** have the **same number of electron shells**.
 
• The periodic table currently contains **118 confirmed elements**, with additional elements being discovered and added over time.
 
• The elements are organized based on their **atomic structure**, with the** number of protons in the nucleus** determining an element's identity.
 
• The table is a powerful tool for understanding the **relationships between different elements **and predicting their** chemical behavior**.
 
• It provides a framework for organizing and studying the properties of elements, as well as for understanding their roles in chemical reactions and compounds.
 
• The periodic table is widely used in chemistry, physics, biology, and other scientific fields.
 
• It has also been influential in the development of new materials and technologies, as well as in the study of the universe and the natural world.
 
• The periodic table has undergone several revisions and updates over the years, reflecting advances in scientific knowledge and the discovery of new elements.
 
• Elements are classified into different categories on the periodic table, including** metals, nonmetals, metalloids, alkali metals, alkaline earth metals, transition metals, halogens, and noble gases**.
 
• The table also includes** lanthanides and actinides,** which are often placed separately at the bottom to conserve space.
 
• Each element on the periodic table is represented by a **chemical symbol**, typically derived from its name in Latin or another language.
 
• The modern periodic table is a fundamental tool for understanding the nature of matter and the behavior of atoms and molecules.
